record.summary: Sets up a controlled testing environment (regulatory sandbox), launched with the European Commission's collaboration, to test how AI systems that may pose risks to safety, health and fundamental rights can meet requirements of the then-proposed EU AI Regulation. Selected providers and users of high-risk systems, general-purpose systems and foundation models implement risk management, data quality, technical documentation, logging, transparency, human oversight, and accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity requirements, self-assess compliance, set up post-market monitoring and report serious incidents. The competent body publishes a report on results, good practices and recommendations.
record.notes: Dated 8 November 2023 and published in BOE No. 268 of 9 November 2023; in force from 10 November 2023, the day after publication. Under its second final provision it was valid for at most 36 months from entry into force, that is to November 2026, or until the EU Regulation laying down harmonised rules on artificial intelligence became applicable in Spain; Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 applies generally from 2 August 2026, with earlier dates for some chapters and a later one for the high-risk rules of Article 6(1). The sandbox took the position of the Council of the EU of 25 November 2022 on the proposed Regulation as its reference, and the Secretary of State for Digitalisation and Artificial Intelligence was the competent body. The pilot, whose call was opened by a resolution of the Secretary of State of 20 December 2024, has finished and its results report has been published. The organic law bill on AI that the Government sent to the Congress in 2026 would expressly repeal the decree, given the obligation to set up a new AI regulatory sandbox under the EU Regulation.

verification.note: Stored and read in this run: the BOE ELI page of the decree (HTML, last checked 17 Oct 2026 and unchanged since 11 Oct 2026) and the BOE PDF of the official text in Spanish (the Catalan PDF is also stored), which confirm the title, the date of 8 November 2023 (Council of Ministers deliberation on 7 November), publication in BOE No. 268 of 9 November 2023 as BOE-A-2023-22767, entry into force on 10 November 2023, the second final provision on validity and the content in the summary; the BOE analysis block gives the validity as 'in the terms of final provision 2' and lists no later references. Also stored: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 on EUR-Lex (Article 113, application from 2 August 2026; EUR-Lex marks the act as changed, consolidated version of 27 July 2026), the ministry's sandbox page (last updated 28 September 2026: the pilot has finished and its results report is published), and the BOCG Congreso text of the organic law bill of 12 June 2026, whose single repealing provision names the decree (congreso.es is not yet listed in pipeline/official-sites.json, so it counts as secondary). The status 'Lapsed' is derived from the validity clause and the Regulation's date of application; no official notice of lapse or repeal was found. The English translation on regalert.today shows the title and preamble in the stored copy, does not name a translator, and lists the CNMV as the issuer, which is wrong (the decree is the Government's). Version 1's statement that the Government continued sandbox calls in 2026 is not supported: the stored ministry page names only the call of 20 December 2024 and says the pilot has finished.

english_version.quote: Royal Decree 817/2023, of November 8, establishing a controlled testing environment for testing compliance with the proposal for a Regulation of the European Parliament and of the Council laying down harmonised rules on artificial intelligence.

judgment.status_reasoning: Rule: the second final provision limits the decree's validity to at most 36 months from entry into force (10 Nov 2023, so to 10 Nov 2026) 'or, where applicable, until the EU Regulation laying down harmonised rules on AI is applicable in Spain'. Event: Article 113 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 says it 'shall apply from 2 August 2026' and is directly applicable in all Member States (some chapters earlier, Article 6(1) high-risk rules from 2027). Arithmetic: 2 Aug 2026 is before today, 17 Oct 2026, so the earlier of the two limits has passed and the decree is no longer valid: 'Lapsed'. Consistent with this, the ministry's page (28 Sep 2026) says the sandbox pilot has finished. The Government's bill of May/June 2026 still lists the decree for express repeal, which fits a decree still valid before 2 Aug 2026. A narrower reading (the decree runs until the high-risk rules it tests apply) would keep it valid to 10 Nov 2026 at the latest; the general date of application is the plain reading. Whichever reading applies, the decree lapses no later than 10 Nov 2026.
judgment.scope_reasoning: Binding implementing decree setting up a national AI regulatory sandbox for compliance testing; in scope without a note.
